title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0RC1RA_0LD0RB_1LA1LF_0LC1RF_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0RC1RA_0LD0RB_1LA1LF_0LC1RF_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Unlike the rest of its group it grows mostly to the right. Its tape is a word of the tokens 1^5 0, 1^6 0^2, 1^7 0 and a few others, ending in a block 1^(2j+1). j grows by one per overflow, at gaps that double, so some binary counter is hidden in the word; from time to time a restructure rewrites the word and j starts again.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps.

What it does. Each time the head reaches a new cell at the right end, in state C, the tape ends in 1^7 0 1^7 0 1^(2j+1) 0 C>0 for most of an epoch. j grows by one each time and the gap doubles exactly. The last four restructures began at steps 2,963,507, 220,322,024, 466,316,545 and 4,568,654,941; in the current epoch the end block has reached 1^61 (step 66,520,947,462), longer than in any earlier epoch.
Why it is hard. Where the counter is, and the restructure rule, are not known, and a closed tape language from short windows does not confine the halt (state F reading a 0).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1011 steps without a halt; 534 cells visited (58 left of the start, 476 right), 382 ones at the end.

claims.title: The right end in the current epoch
claims.text: From step 4,568,656,718 to 66,520,947,462 the head reached a new cell at the right end in state C 28 times, two cells each time. The tape then ended in 1^7 0 1^7 0 1^k 0 C>0 with k = 7, 9, …, 61, one step of 2 each time. The gap between successive times doubled exactly at the last 11 of them (ratio 2.0000 to four digits).

claims.title: Restructures
claims.text: The end block falls back to a few cells many times in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps, often in bursts of two or three falls within a few thousand steps. The last four bursts began at steps 2,963,507, 220,322,024, 466,316,545 and 4,568,654,941, after end blocks of 27, 43, 35 and 53 cells; the left end of the tape moved shortly before the last three.

claims.title: A hidden binary counter
claims.text: A unary block that grows by one unit while the time doubles means that the run counts in binary somewhere else on the tape, presumably in the word on the left, and lengthens the end block at each overflow.

claims.title: The restructures, and the question itself
claims.text: Not known: where the counter is, what triggers a restructure, the rule that rebuilds the word, and whether the machine halts.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping. The block of 1s at its right end grows by two cells each time a hidden counter overflows, at doubling gaps, until a restructure rewrites the tape. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 534 cells visited.
The end block at step 66,520,947,462, the longest so far.
The gap between growths of the end block doubles.

sections.heading: A block that grows while time doubles
html:
Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the right end. In the current epoch, which began at step 4,568,654,941, the tape then ends in 1^7 0 1^7 0 1^k 0 C>0, and k grows by 2 each time:

stepend blockgap
12,312,693,2461^553,872,018,052
20,056,729,4661^577,744,036,220
35,544,801,9481^5915,488,072,482
66,520,947,4621^6130,976,145,514

The gap doubles each time, so a binary counter overflows somewhere else on the tape and each overflow lengthens the end block by two cells. The rest of the tape is a word of the tokens 1^5 0, 1^6 0^2, 1^7 0 and some others.

sections.heading: Restructures
html:
From time to time the end block falls back to a few cells and the word in front of it is rewritten: many times in the first 1011 steps, often in bursts of two or three. The last four bursts began at steps 2,963,507, 220,322,024, 466,316,545 and 4,568,654,941, after end blocks of 27, 43, 35 and 53 cells. The current epoch has reached 61 cells, and its next overflow is due near 1.3·1011 steps.

The machine halts only in state F reading a 0. A closed tape language from short windows does not show where that could happen, and nothing is known about when a restructure comes or what it writes.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073).
After 109 steps the tape spans 459 cells (55 left of the start, 397 right), with a density of 1s of 0.747.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: counter with a unary end block, gaps doubling, and restructures
summary: Open. No halt in 10^11 steps. Most of the time the block of 1s at the right end grows by two cells per overflow while the gap between overflows doubles; at irregular restructures the end block falls back to a few cells and the word in front of it is rewritten.
